fact: Morocco's customs administration (ADII), with the World Customs Organization and Swiss SECO, launched a project on 19 May 2025 to integrate AI into customs risk analysis and targeting, and a first technical mission ran 19-23 May 2025 assessing current capacity.

fact: Morocco's Customs and Indirect Taxes Administration has implemented pilot projects using machine learning on customs declarations to identify fraud risks, with further testing underway, per the budget minister's written answer.
Le360, citing expert Marouane Harmach, reports that the Direction generale des impots is deploying AI in fraud detection.

The Pôle Digital de l'Agriculture, de la Forêt et Observatoire de la Sécheresse announced on 6 March 2024 the signing of an agreement with Russian firm BTI Group for a proof of concept using satellites and AI for crop recognition, parcel delineation and water consumption, at the R'Mel irrigated perimeter (Loukkos) and the commune of Ait Harz Allah (El Hajeb).
system: POC satellites et IA (Pôle Digital de l'Agriculture / BTI Group)

fact: Maroc.ma (MAP) reports the Moroccan Medicines and Health Products Agency launched the Tarkhiss platform on 31 March 2026, which includes AI-based analysis tools to process files, starting with cosmetics and body-hygiene products for about 3,500 operators.

Le Matin, citing a parliamentary working group report, says an AI system for school support management is deployed in the Draa-Tafilalet Academy, using the Massar, SAGE+ and GEXA+ databases to predict pupil performance and flag dropout risk.
The 7News report says authorities are working to introduce artificial intelligence into PortNet, Morocco's customs single window, with no tool yet in service.

Morocco's customs administration (ADII) reports that in 2024 its BADR system, described as applied artificial intelligence, processed 1,540 fraud alerts and was enriched by 434 new rules and 199 updates, alongside predictive algorithms for targeting.
The ADII 2024 activity report says algorithm-based targeting detected 34 MDH of evaded duties and taxes (24 MDH in 2023), of which 20 MDH was recovered and 14 MDH levied as fines.
